title: FENa vs FEUrea in AKI
subtitle: Distinguish prerenal from intrinsic renal injury

steps.title: When to use FENa
steps.body: Fractional excretion of sodium helps differentiate prerenal azotemia from ATN in oliguric patients NOT on diuretics.
steps.tip: FENa = (Urine Na × Plasma Cr) / (Plasma Na × Urine Cr) × 100.

steps.title: Interpret FENa
steps.body: FENa <1% suggests prerenal physiology. FENa >2% strongly favors ATN. Values 1–2% are indeterminate.
steps.tip: Also expect BUN:Cr >20:1 and urine osm >500 in prerenal.

steps.title: Limitation — diuretics
steps.body: Loop or thiazide diuretics increase urine sodium and make FENa unreliable even when patient is prerenal.
steps.tip: If on diuretics, use FEUrea instead.

steps.title: Use FEUrea
steps.body: FEUrea <35% favors prerenal; ≥50% favors intrinsic renal injury. Less affected by diuretics than FENa.
steps.tip: FEUrea = (Urine urea × Plasma Cr) / (Plasma urea × Urine Cr) × 100.

steps.title: Clinical integration
steps.body: Combine indices with history, exam, urine microscopy (muddy brown casts in ATN), and response to volume challenge.
steps.tip: Prerenal AKI should improve within 24–48 h of perfusion restoration.
